transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I guess the main thing is that I just stopped caring about everything I used to look forward to. My fishing gear is still sitting untouched out in the garage, and going out to the woodshop just feels like a chore now. Even when my kids try to get me to play chess with them, I’m really just going through the motions. I don't get anything out of it anymore. So, I figured I needed to come in.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest in the things you usually enjoy?

It's been a while now. I'd say... about a year and seven months. That's when my wife started having health problems, and it really just changed everything at home. Ever since then, I just haven't been able to get into anything.
Do you feel this started because of the stress of your wife’s health problems?

I'm not really sure. I mean, it was definitely a stressful time, obviously, but I don't know if that's what actually caused it. I just know that's right around the time everything kind of went flat for me.
During this past year and seven months, have you felt this way nearly every day the whole time?

Yeah, I'd say so. Pretty much every day. I mean, I guess there might have been a day here or there where I was just too busy at work to notice, but... no, it's been pretty constant. I just wake up and it's that same flat feeling, every single day.
During this time, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

Not really. I mean... I wouldn't say I feel sad or down, exactly. It's not like I'm sitting around crying or anything like that. It's mostly just that flat feeling I was talking about. I just don't really feel much of anything.
Do you feel your lack of interest is mainly because of the stress around your wife’s health problems?

I really couldn't say for sure. Like I mentioned a minute ago, the timing definitely lines up with when she got sick, so maybe it played a part. But I don't know if that stress is the main reason I don't care about things anymore. It's just... I just don't have any interest in much of anything these days, and I honestly don't know exactly why.
Over the past year and seven months, have you felt hopeless most days?

No, I wouldn't say hopeless. I don't really sit around thinking things are doomed or that the future is bleak or anything like that. It's really just that flat feeling I mentioned. I just feel empty, not hopeless.
Has this loss of interest been causing problems in your day-to-day life?

Yeah, it definitely is. At work, I've started missing things. I manage construction sites, so you can't really afford to do that—it affects deadlines and, more importantly, safety. We actually had a near-miss recently, and after that happened, I realized I couldn't just pretend it was only stress anymore. 

And it's affecting things at home, too. I mean, I'm there physically, but that's about it. My wife and kids are basically having to work around me now, instead of being able to count on me the way they used to.
During this past year and seven months, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when, in addition to losing interest, you also felt depressed or down most of the day nearly every day?

No, I haven't really felt down or sad like that. I know people usually think of being depressed as crying all the time or feeling miserable, but that's not it for me. It's just that emptiness. I haven't had any stretches where I felt specifically sad or depressed, just... flat.
During this time, have you been feeling worthless or like you’re not good enough?

Yeah, I have. A lot, actually. I just keep thinking that I've completely failed my wife, my kids... and the guys at work, too. It's like, if anything goes wrong—if there's a missed appointment at home, or a cost overrun on a project, or especially a safety issue on site—I just take it as proof that I'm completely useless. I really feel like everyone would just be better off without me in charge of things.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of killing yourself?

Yeah, I have. I mean... on those early drives to the sites, before anyone else is even awake, I catch myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't make it there. And sometimes, the thought of just steering off the road crosses my mind. It actually scares me when that happens, because it feels a little too close.
Are you intending to kill yourself?

No, I'm not. I don't... I don't actually have a plan to do it or anything like that. Like I said, the thought just kind of flashes through my mind and it really scares me when it does. I wouldn't actually go through with it. I think I just... I just want the pressure to stop.
During this time, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when your sleep was clearly different than usual?

Yeah, my sleep has been pretty bad for a while now. I mean, I can get into bed completely exhausted from the day, but then I just lie there. My mind keeps running through bills, schedules, everything going on at work. And even if I do fall asleep, I end up waking up around three or four in the morning. Then I just stare at the ceiling until it's time to get up and drive to the site. It's been happening pretty much every night for weeks.
During the past year and seven months, was there ever a stretch of two months or longer when these symptoms mostly went away?

No, I don't think so. It hasn't really let up at all. I mean... maybe there's a day here or there where I'm just too busy on a site to dwell on it, but definitely not a stretch of two whole months. It's been pretty constant this whole time.
During this time, have you had low self-esteem?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really... I don't feel bad about myself as a person, if that's what you mean. I know I'm good at my job, and I know what I'm doing when I'm managing a site. So, no, it's not really an issue with my self-esteem.
